notes: Identity assessed independently from the supplied text: title page names The impact of Screen Time, Social Media Use and Extraversion on Life Satisfaction among University Students: An extended replication study; Sara von Pruski; Department of Psychology, University of Twente; Bachelor Thesis; date 01.07.2024. Supplied source URL identifies essay.utwente.nl file/100459, agreeing with the neutral reference identifier. This is the primary thesis report, with results, discussion, references and appendices through PDF page 78, rather than an abstract-only parse or preregistration. No DOI is printed for this thesis. No source PDF path was supplied, so PDF layout was not independently rendered. Target remains ambiguous: description does not distinguish passive social media use, active social media use, or total screen time, nor bivariate, multiple regression, parallel mediation, or moderation tests. P.29 moderation prints total screen time B=-0.09, SE=0.19, t(3,94)=-0.47, p=.64; total screen time includes non-social-media activities. P.28 Table 3 conditional paths to life satisfaction print TST B=-0.16, SE=0.18, t=-0.91, p=.36; PSMU B=-0.09, SE=0.15, t=-0.64, p=.53; ASMU B=0.08, SE=0.11, t=0.68, p=.5. Table 2 also prints LS/PSMU r=.01 and LS/ASMU r=.02 without same-test exact p values (no stars). No coefficient is selected from these candidates. Authors say the direct effects were contrary to expectations but no indirect effects agreed with Bunz; this does not establish a unique replication verdict for the broad assigned relationship. Analytic N unresolved: p.20 reports 149 recruited, not a critical-model analytic N. P.24 retains incomplete cases in the dataset; p.35 states missing values were automatically removed from analyses. P.35 refers to sample size 92 in the multiple regression discussion and 94 for the moderation interaction, while p.36 describes current samples varying between 91 and 94. These are candidate author-labelled sample counts only; exact target correspondence and the mediation sample are not independently established. No N inferred from df, recruitment count, code execution, or arithmetic. Only assigned unfinished fields were assessed. Unassigned original and p fields are placeholders.
